name: banking_intents
description: Customer messages sent to a retail bank's chat assistant, each labelled with the customer's primary intent. Used to train and evaluate an intent classifier.
context:
Customers write on mobile, often tersely, sometimes emotionally, with typos, slang, and missing
punctuation. Many messages mention amounts, merchants, dates or card types. Some customers
write long, rambling messages with backstory; others send three words. Non-native English
speakers are common. Messages never contain real card numbers; if a number appears it is
masked (e.g. "card ending 4417").

fields.name: text
fields.description: The customer's message, exactly as they typed it.

fields.name: secondary_intent
fields.description: A second intent if the message clearly contains one, else null.

rules: The text must express the labelled intent clearly enough that a careful human annotator agrees with it, except in edge-case slots, where it may be ambiguous but the label must still be the best choice.
fraud_alert and card_lost_or_stolen messages usually have urgency 4-5.
Do not mention the intent label or category names verbatim in the text.
checks: secondary_intent is None or secondary_intent != intent

diversity.scenario_guidance: Vary customer demographics, life situations (travel abroad, new job, small business owner, student, retiree), emotional states, message lengths and writing styles.
